headline: Denmark's finance minister says Ireland's EU budget plan cuts the wrong things
headline_short: Denmark rejects Irish EU budget plan
deck: The plan trims the overall budget by 8 per cent but farming and regional aid by only 3; Germany objects too.
standard: Peter Hummelgaard, Denmark's finance minister, has rejected Ireland's proposal for the EU's budget for 2028 to 2034. 'The budget is still too high, and the proposed cuts have the wrong focus,' he said. Germany has also rejected it.

Ireland, which holds the EU's rotating presidency, presented the plan on Saturday. It cuts the European Commission's draft by 8 per cent, but farming, fisheries and regional development by only 3 per cent; competitiveness, prosperity and security lose 13 per cent.

Hummelgaard wants less spent on farming and regional aid. Ireland is among about 20 countries that want such transfers kept high; Thomas Byrne, its Europe minister, said Ireland had been 'an honest broker'.
short: Peter Hummelgaard, Denmark's finance minister, has rejected the plan from Ireland, which holds the EU's rotating presidency, for the 2028 to 2034 budget, saying it is still too high and cuts the wrong things. It trims the European Commission's draft by 8 per cent but farming, fisheries and regional development by only 3 per cent.
